Some tax-free government payments may also need to be declared because they can affect your eligibility for tax offsets and other benefits. ## Income tax offsets, levies and surcharges ### Medicare levy+ You pay this levy in addition to the tax you pay on your taxable income. For families eligible for SAPTO, the thresholds are $61,623 and $77,028 respectively.

## What You Can Work Out With This Pay Calculator
### Tax, study debt, and offsets
PAYG income tax applies bracket by bracket, the Low Income Tax Offset trims the bill at lower incomes, and the Medicare Levy adds its shade-in band — the breakdown shows each, plus an optional [HECS/HELP repayment](https://www.wagecalculator.com.au/hecs-calculator) once income exceeds the compulsory threshold. The [Australian income tax guide](https://www.wagecalculator.com.au/guides/australia-income-tax) walks through how each component is calculated, and at tax time the [tax return calculator](https://www.wagecalculator.com.au/tax-return-calculator) estimates your refund or amount owing from the same components.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### How is income tax calculated in Australia?
The brackets for the current financial year are: 0% on income up to $18,200 (the tax-free threshold), 15% on $18,201–$45,000, 30% on $45,001–$135,000, 37% on $135,001–$190,000, 45% on income above $190,000. This pay calculator applies all current brackets, LITO, and the Medicare Levy automatically based on the income entered.

### How much tax do I pay on $100,000 in Australia?
For a $100,000 gross salary the estimated income tax is approximately $20,520 plus a Medicare Levy of $2,000 — an effective combined rate of about 22.5% for the current financial year. Net take-home is roughly $77,480 per year. At this income level the Medicare Levy Surcharge may apply if no private hospital cover is held, and a HECS debt would add the compulsory repayment for the relevant band on top.
